notes.title: June Update
notes.content:
I made an update to my game today of the run speed today.  Shift key allows you to move faster than the horror game walk that you begin with.   

There is still a short lived sugar rush burst of energy you get from eating cookies, but you still have to bide your time and strategize how you eat your cookies.

Don't forget you can use the 1-6 keys to dial in higher or lower resolution whenever you want, that may be more suitable for your computer. 

Beware the cats. Beware the sugar rush when you are in places you might not want it.

Always beware the cats.

notes.title: Studio Update : Collider Fixes, Cleaner Game Start, and Sugar Rush
notes.content:
I added a few things to clean up my game today, some collider fixes to the first level that I noticed were broken.  I also removed the list of hot keys at the start of the game ( it is in the titles and can be accessed with the tab key which I tell about a minute into the game).

It was a little overwhelming to have the title, the brief instructions come up and then the image to instantly get slammed with the hot  key list.   It's still accessible, but I just wanted a cleaner start to the game. 

I also have been experimenting with other things in the game in terms of gameplay.  I experimented (and programmed) falling damage. I then removed it preferring to keep the simple horror (you die after eaten) philosophy of my game.

I did however add a small reward in the game.  After you eat a cookie you get a bonus, what I call a sugar rush from the cookie.  You can run really fast for about six seconds.  However, as all good things must pass, this will become less time with the more cookies you eat.  The message is you should eat better of course...  stop relying on a sugar rush from cookies to get you through the cat zombie apocalypse!!! 

-Daev

notes.title: The Studio Update : New Models & Other small things
notes.content:
I put some things in my game to move things a little more, some things that i had hidden I've brought more to the fore.

There are new models I've worked on, my homage to Skyrim.  I also just returned from New Jersey where I saw the Creepy Clown of Middletown in person with my sons.   It was the first time they had seen it in person, although they're very familiar with it from my game.  This is part of the game I brought to the foreground a little more.

notes.title: The Studio Update : Hide Grass : Pause Key and Shadow improvements
notes.content:
I posted two updates of the Studio in the last couple days.  One for some chattering of shadows I noticed in Pumpkin castle.   This is caused by bias issues within Unreal game engine and I adjusted to be less accurate more forgiving .  When testing the game there are different places I can test.  In the game engine or even from my system the shadows don't appear to be an issue, however when loaded up through steam they showed the weakness that I needed to address.  This should clear up most of the chattering. I will refine this more with future versions.  

Additionally, I was told there is lagging on some systems.  I'm trying to address lagging, but this is  a bigger can of worms than I can't address in a quick update.

I have however added a hotkey if you find it lagging. The H key (for hide) will hide or rather toggle the grass on or off in the game. There should be a increase in frame rate from this drop.  I'm going to keep finessing the not so quick stuff though to improve gameplay. 

Finally, I've added a Pause key as requested.  The P-key will Pause and Un-pause game play so you can go eat dinner, or take a pee break, your choice.

As always me and my team will do our best to make game play enjoyable. Okay, I don't really have a "team".  It's just me behind the scenes trying to make a game that people may enjoy.   

best
Daev
